{
  "patch": "*** Begin Patch\n*** Add File: /private/tmp/reigh-chain-workspace/reigh-app/docs/structure_detail/state_ownership.md\n+## Purpose\n+State ownership keeps each concern writable in one place, which is how we exit the M1-M6 mirror pattern that copied the same meaning across React Query, zustand, and Context. The rule for this cleanup is simple: server-backed facts stay in RQ, ephemeral UI stays in zustand, provider-scoped handles stay in Context, and readers consume the owner instead of syncing mirrors.\n+\n+## Source-of-truth table\n+| Owner | Use for | Must not mirror into |\n+| --- | --- | --- |\n+| RQ | Server-backed data, fetch lifecycle, invalidation | zustand setters fed by `useEffect`, duplicate Context copies of fetched records |\n+| zustand | Ephemeral UI state, local toggles, pane locks, open flags | RQ cache mirrors, parallel Context state for the same UI concern |\n+| Context | Provider-scoped handles, imperative APIs, composition boundaries | duplicate zustand stores for the same handles, copied server data snapshots |\n+\n+## Three do-nots\n+1. Bad: `useEffect(() => setStore(query.data), [query.data])`\n+   Good: read `query.data` where needed, or move the concern fully into the store if it is truly local UI state.\n+2. Bad: register an overlay when a ref attaches, even while the overlay is closed.\n+   Good: gate registration on explicit `open` state so mount timing does not become the source of truth.\n+3. Bad: keep a Context hook beside a zustand store that holds the same pane-lock state.\n+   Good: keep one owner and expose selectors or provider handles around it; this cleanup deletes the duplicate pane-lock hook pattern.\n+\n+## Pointer\n+For worked M7 examples, inspect `git log megaplan/m7-state-cleanup`. Collapsed bootstrap and overlay-open tradeoffs are intentionally deferred to M7B+.\n*** End Patch\n"
}
```
